newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ALOMAR AND UMPIRE HE SPAT ON SHAKE HANDS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ALOMAR AND UMPIRE HE SPAT ON SHAKE HANDS.

text.p: With a handshake before Tuesday night's game, Baltimore Orioles second baseman Roberto Alomar and American League umpire John Hirschbeck tried to get past one of the uglier incidents in baseball's recent history.

The two were on the same field tonight at Baltimore's Oriole Park at Camden Yards for the first time since last September 27th, when Alomar spit in Hirschbeck's face in a game between the Orioles and Toronto Blue Jays.

Alomar was suspended five games for the incident, but the suspension did not take effect until the 1997 season. The umpires thought Alomar had received scant punishment and they threatened a walkout in the last season's American League Division Playoffs.
The spitting incident sparked an ugly verbal and legal battle between umpires and players. The umpires were incensed that Alomar did not have to serve his suspension in the postseason.

Alomar was sidelined most of spring training with a left ankle injury and might have missed the start of the season even without the suspension. Hirschbeck worked a spring training game involving the Orioles while Alomar was sidelined.
Alomar hit .328 with 22 homers and 94 RBI and was named to the AL All-Star team last season. He went 1-for-3 with a walk Tuesday, raising his average to .257.
